messages:
Maya: thinking aloud — in the rollout wizard, can we add a "safe switch" preview that shows exactly what would happen if a trigger fires? feels risky to let people flip fallback rules without a dry-run
Carla: yes pls. we need a deterministic preview so SREs can eyeball the change. even a single sample trace would help :eyes:
Jonathan: +1. also needs to show who can override and for how long. operator overrides should be auditable with TTLs
Sam: idea: preview mode runs the policy against a small replay of recent traffic and shows matches/hits count. no side effects, just a report
Dinesh: replay is good but expensive. can we do "synthetic sampling" where we synthesize the request envelope and run through the decision path? cheaper and faster
Maya: agree on synthetic sampling. UX should show a few example requests and the resulting action (route/model change/degrade) side-by-side
Carla: sketch of the config UI snippet for the expert panel (for the backend team to implement):
```yaml
safe_switch:
  dry_run: true
  replay_window: 1h
  sample_count: 20
  audit: true
  override:
    ttl_seconds: 600
    roles_allowed: ["ops","platform-admin"]
triggers:
  - name: p99_latency_spike
    metric: p99_latency_ms
    threshold: 500
    window: 1m
  - name: error_rate_kicker
    metric: server_error_rate
    threshold_percent: 3
    window: 2m
actions:
  - degrade_mode: fallback_to_small_model
    target: model-a-quant
    sample_pct: 25
  - degrade_mode: circuit_open
    scope: route
```
Maya: good. question: how do we surface the audit log? a downloadable diff, or inline timeline in the rollout card?
Jonathan: inline timeline + a downloadable JSON of the exact decision events. must include the rule id, matched condition, and sample input. retention policy configurable (30/90/365 days)
Sam: also add an "explain" button that shows the decision tree for a single sample — like path: metric->threshold->action. That helps PMs when they ask why customers were routed differently
Dinesh: edge case: if the policy uses KV-cache or prefix-caching heuristics, the preview should indicate when cached responses would have been used. otherwise preview can be misleading
Carla: operator UX: require a short rationale text when enabling overrides (free text) and add a required checkbox "I understand this may affect latency/cost". store rationale in audit entry
Maya: permissions question — should engineers be able to create but not activate safe-switches? we need separation between author and activator
Jonathan: yep. RBAC: edit/create -> roles: platform-devs, activate -> roles: platform-ops + managers. activation generates an immutable audit entry with signer identity
ops-bot: NOTE: when a policy activates, ops-bot will emit a channel alert and pin an automated runbook link. can wire to the existing runbook id field
deploy-bot: DEPLOY LOG: simulated dry-run executed at 1705012400 for policy safe_switch:sample run complete. 8/20 samples matched p99_latency_spike action:fallback_to_small_model
Sam: tiny UX nit: show expected cost delta in the preview (est. tokens and cost savings for fallback model) so teams can weigh quality vs cost immediately
Maya: love that. also include rollback button on the rollout card that documents who clicked it and why, plus a required pre-rollback checklist
Dinesh: telemetry: add a dimension `preview_hit_rate` and `override_ttl_used` so we can tune default TTLs over time
Carla: implementation note: backend should return a compact list of decisions for the preview, not full traces. frontend can expand an event on demand to fetch the sample payload
Maya: next steps: engineering - estimate effort for replay vs synthetic sampling; design - mockup the sample comparison panel; security - define RBAC for create/activate/override. I'll compile this into the rollout RFC by EOD
Jonathan: thanks — ping me for RBAC rules. I can write a PoC schema for the audit entries
Sam: +1, i'll volunteer to help the frontend mockups
Maya: awesome. tagging followups: @Carla for sample UI copy, @Dinesh for preview semantics, @Jonathan for audit schema. :thumbsup:
